result.noRegion.diia:
Plates of the DІ series are issued when a vehicle is re-registered online through Diia, instead of at a service centre (TSC).
What is Diia — Ukraine's state app and portal for e-services (documents, registers, vehicle services).
What registering via Diia means — the new owner re-registers the vehicle remotely, with the sale contract concluded through e-services, and gets a plate of the DІ series.
Why there is no region — the letters show how the service was ordered, not where the car is registered, so the plate says nothing about the owner's oblast.
result.noRegion.driverCabinet:
Plates of the ЕD series are issued when a vehicle is re-registered through the Driver's Cabinet (the MIA's online service) instead of at a service centre (TSC).
What is the Driver's Cabinet — the Ministry of Internal Affairs' online account for drivers and vehicle owners.
Why there is no region — the letters show how the service was ordered, not where the car is registered, so the plate says nothing about the owner's oblast.
result.noRegion.generic:
The first letters of this plate are not a regional code, so we cannot tell the region. Typical reasons:
Online-service series — DІ (Diia) and ЕD (Driver's Cabinet) plates carry the service channel, not a region.
Temporary, transit or customs plates — issued for a limited period and not tied to an oblast.
Foreign or non-standard plates — a different country's or an unusual format.
Registry data noise — a typo or an unusual entry in the source open data.
result.notFound.hintPlate: The plate format is valid, but it isn't in the registry data. Either the vehicle was registered before January 2013 (not covered by the open data), or after 29 April 2026 — since May 2026 the registry no longer publishes plates, so those vehicles can only be found by VIN. Plates are in the database for January 2013 – 29 April 2026.
result.notFound.hintFormat: This doesn't look like a complete Ukrainian plate (e.g. AA1234BB). Check for typos.
result.plateInferredHint: The plate number hasn't been published since May 2026 (plates are in the database up to 29 April 2026); this one was reconstructed from the VIN's earlier registrations.

field.about.body:
Body type exactly as written in the registry (Ukrainian names). A suffix like “-B” is the driving-licence category the vehicle falls under (A motorcycle, B car, C truck, D bus, E with trailer).
СЕДАН (sedan) — separate boot, usually 4 doors
ХЕТЧБЕК (hatchback) — boot shares the cabin, rear tailgate
УНІВЕРСАЛ / КОМБІ (wagon) — long roof, large load space
КУПЕ (coupe) — two doors, sporty roofline
ПІКАП (pickup) — open cargo bed behind the cab
ПАСАЖИРСЬКИЙ (passenger) — minivan or passenger van for 5+ seats
ВАНТАЖОПАСАЖИРСЬКИЙ (cargo-passenger) — van with seats and a cargo area
ФУРГОН (van) — closed cargo box; МАЛОТОНАЖНИЙ = light-duty; РЕФРИЖЕРАТОР = refrigerated
БОРТОВИЙ / ТЕНТОВАНИЙ — flatbed truck, open or with a tarpaulin cover
САМОСКИД (dump truck) — tipping cargo bed
СІДЛОВИЙ ТЯГАЧ (tractor unit) — pulls a semi-trailer
АВТОБУС / МІКРОАВТОБУС (bus / minibus) — carries passengers
МОТОЦИКЛ / МОПЕД (motorcycle / moped) — two-wheelers
ПР- (trailer) — towed behind a vehicle, e.g. ПР-БОРТОВИЙ flatbed trailer, ПР-ЛЕГКОВИЙ car trailer
Н/ПР- (semi-trailer) — rests partly on the tractor unit, e.g. Н/ПР-КОНТЕЙНЕРОВОЗ container carrier
ПЛАТФОРМА (platform) — flat load deck without sides
field.about.capacity:
Engine displacement — the total volume of all cylinders, in cubic centimetres (cc). Roughly: more cc, more power and more fuel.
Up to 1000 cc — city cars
1000–1600 cc — everyday family cars
1600–2500 cc — larger cars and SUVs
2500 cc and up — powerful or heavy vehicles. In Ukraine the import customs duty and the luxury tax depend on it.
field.about.power:
Peak engine power in kilowatts (kW). 1 kW ≈ 1.34 hp. Shown for vehicles registered since 2026; for an electric car it replaces the engine capacity.
50 kW — ≈ 67 hp
100 kW — ≈ 134 hp
150 kW — ≈ 201 hp
field.about.color: The body colour recorded at registration. It is what the owner or dealer declared and can differ from the real colour after a repaint — a repaint should be re-registered, but often isn’t.
field.about.fuel:
The fuel the engine runs on, as registered.
Gasoline (petrol) and diesel — the most common
Gas / LPG — a petrol car converted to run on gas (often bi-fuel)
Electric — battery only, no engine capacity
Hybrid — combustion engine plus an electric motor
field.about.weight:
Two figures in kilograms (kg), separated by a slash.
Kerb weight — the empty vehicle with fluids, without driver, passengers or cargo
Gross weight — the maximum permitted weight when fully loaded. The difference is the payload.
field.about.kind: The vehicle class from the registration papers: passenger car, truck, bus, motorcycle, trailer, etc. Together with the body type it tells what the vehicle is meant to do.
field.about.purpose: What the vehicle is registered for: general use, taxi, special services, rent, training, etc. A “taxi” or “training” purpose is a hint of intensive past use.
field.about.ownersCount: Estimated number of owners: the first registration plus every re-registration due to a change of owner. The registry holds no identity data, so this is an estimate: a sale without re-registration is invisible, and history only starts in 2013.
field.about.owner: Whether the current owner is a private person or a legal entity (company). The registry never shows names or any personal data.
field.about.regDate: The date of the latest registration operation in the registry — the first registration, a re-registration after a sale, or a change of data. It is not necessarily the date the car was built or first sold. The full chain is in the history below.
field.about.dep: The MVS service centre (ТСЦ МВС) that carried out the latest registration. Tap it to see it on the map.
field.about.koatuu:
KOATUU — the old Ukrainian classifier of administrative-territorial units. A 10-digit code of the settlement where the owner is registered (it names the place, not the street address).
Digits 1–2 — oblast (48 Mykolaiv, 63 Kharkiv, 80 Kyiv city…); the app shows its name next to the code
Digits 3–5 — district or city of oblast significance
Digits 6–8 — settlement or village council
Digits 9–10 — the settlement itself
Example: 4823355100 → Mykolaiv Oblast (48), then district, council and settlement
field.about.vin: Vehicle Identification Number — a unique 17-character code of the car, like its passport number. It stays with the car for life, unlike the plate. Open it to decode the maker, year, engine and more.
section.about.vin:
Everything the 17-character VIN reveals about the car, decoded by the free US NHTSA database and our registry.
Parts of the VIN — manufacturer, model descriptor, check digit, model year, plant, serial number
Specs — body, drive, engine, transmission, safety equipment
Less data for cars made for the European market — NHTSA covers US-market vehicles best
section.about.history:
Every registration operation on record for this plate and for this VIN, newest first.
First registration, re-registration after a sale, change of colour, engine or documents
Plate history — everyone who ever wore this plate, including reassignments
VIN history — every plate this one vehicle has had
Only operations from 2013 onward are in the open data
section.about.emissions:
Estimated fuel use and CO₂ for this make, model, year and engine — reference data, not a measurement of this particular car.
EPA — the US fuel-economy database
EEA — official EU type-approval CO₂ data (2010+)
The lower the g/km of CO₂ and the litres per 100 km, the cheaper and cleaner the car is to run
section.about.photos:
Stock photos of this make and model from Pixabay, to give a rough idea of the look.
Illustrative only — not this specific car, so colour, trim and condition will differ
May show other generations or be empty for rare models
section.about.wiki:
A short summary of the make and model from Wikipedia, with a photo and a link to the full article.
It describes the model in general — generation, history, specs — not this specific car
The language follows the app language when an article exists, otherwise English
section.about.nearby:
A Google Maps search around your current location for services this car may need.
Mechanics — repair shops and service stations
Brand dealers — official dealers of this make
Insurance — insurance agents
The browser asks for your location when you open the section; it is only used for the map and is not stored
section.about.videos:
Video reviews and test drives for this make and model, matched to this car's model and year.
Videos come from infocar.ua's video section and play from YouTube — nothing loads from YouTube until you press a video
We only link to the videos and do not copy them
section.about.reviews:
Written reviews and owner stories for this make and model, grouped by source.
infocar.ua — test drives and owner reviews, matched to this car's model and year
e-drive.com.ua — owners' own logbook posts (repairs, service, accessories) from this car's generation, not professional reviews
Other sites — search results for this make and model
We only link out to these sites and do not copy their content

vin.details.title: All details
vin.info.descriptor: The model-specific part of the VIN (positions 4–9) with the unknown characters replaced by *, plus the year and plant codes.
vin.info.manufacturer: The legal entity that built the vehicle. It can differ from the brand on the badge (e.g. a corporation owning several makes).
vin.info.series: A sub-model or body-style detail that the manufacturer encodes in the VIN.
vin.info.trim: The equipment level of this model, e.g. LX, EX, Limited.
vin.info.vehicleType: Regulatory class: passenger car, multipurpose passenger vehicle (SUV/MPV), truck, bus, trailer, motorcycle…
vin.info.bodyClass: The body shape: sedan, hatchback, wagon, SUV, pickup…
vin.info.doors: Number of doors, counting a hatchback or tailgate as one.
vin.info.driveType: Which wheels the engine drives: FWD (front), RWD (rear), AWD/4WD (all four).
vin.info.transmission:
How engine power reaches the wheels.
Manual (MT) — you shift gears with a clutch pedal; simple, cheap, durable
Automatic (AT) — torque-converter gearbox with 6–10 speeds; smooth and tough (Toyota, BMW’s ZF 8-speed)
CVT — belt and pulleys with no fixed gears; very smooth and economical but can feel “rubbery” (Nissan, Subaru, Toyota, Hyundai)
DCT / DSG (dual-clutch) — two clutches for fast shifts (VW DSG, Ford PowerShift); efficient but can be jerky at low speed
AMT (automated manual) — manual gearbox shifted by a robot; cheap, slow shifts (older Fiat, Opel Easytronic)
Electric cars use a single-speed reduction gear.
vin.info.gvwr:
Gross vehicle weight rating: the maximum safe loaded weight (car + fuel + passengers + cargo) set by the manufacturer. NHTSA groups it into US classes 1–8:
Class 1 — up to 6,000 lb (2,722 kg): cars, small SUVs, minivans (Corolla, Golf, Honda CR-V)
Class 2 — 6,001–10,000 lb (up to 4,536 kg): full-size pickups and vans (Ford F-150, Sprinter)
Class 3 — 10,001–14,000 lb (up to 6,350 kg): heavy-duty pickups, large vans (Ford F-350)
Class 4–6 — up to 26,000 lb (11,793 kg): delivery and box trucks
Class 7–8 — over 26,000 lb: semi-trucks, buses, heavy haulage
vin.info.cylinders:
Number of engine cylinders — the chambers where fuel burns and pushes the pistons. More cylinders usually means smoother and more powerful, but thirstier.
2–3 — tiny city engines (Fiat 500 TwinAir, Ford EcoSport 1.0, Toyota Aygo)
4 — the everyday standard (VW Golf 1.5, Kia Ceed 1.6, Toyota Corolla 1.8)
5 — rarer, distinctive sound (Audi RS3, older Volvo T5)
6 — V6 or in-line six, smooth and strong (BMW M340i, Toyota Camry 3.5)
8 — V8, big power and torque (Ford Mustang GT, Mercedes E63)
12 — luxury and supercars (Ferrari 812, Rolls-Royce Phantom)
vin.info.displacement:
Total volume swept by all pistons — the “engine size”. Bigger usually means more power and torque, and more fuel burnt. 1000 cc = 1 litre ≈ 61 cubic inches.
1.0–1.4 L — small city cars (Hyundai i10, VW Polo)
1.5–2.0 L — typical family cars (Kia Ceed, Toyota Corolla, VW Golf)
2.5–3.5 L — larger sedans and SUVs (Toyota Camry, Ford Explorer)
4.0 L and up — V8 trucks and performance cars (Ford F-150, Mercedes E63)
Turbo engines get more power from less volume: a 1.5 L turbo can match an older 2.0 L.
vin.info.engineModel:
The manufacturer’s engine family name or code. It tells you the generation and design — handy for finding parts, known issues and service intervals. A trailing II / III usually means a later generation.
Gamma / Gamma II — Hyundai-Kia 1.4–1.6 L four-cylinder petrol (Kia Ceed, Rio, Hyundai Elantra, Solaris)
Theta II — Hyundai-Kia 2.0–2.4 L petrol (Sonata, Optima, Sportage)
EcoBoost — Ford turbo petrol family, 1.0 L three-cylinder to 3.5 L V6
TSI / TFSI — VW-Audi turbo petrol (Golf, Octavia, Audi A3)
Dynamic Force — Toyota 2.0–2.5 L petrol (Corolla, Camry, RAV4)
K-series — Honda 2.0–2.4 L petrol (Civic Si, Accord, CR-V)
B48 / N20 — BMW turbo four-cylinders
vin.info.engineConfig:
Cylinder layout of the engine.
In-line (I3, I4, I6) — one row of cylinders; simple and compact, most four-cylinders
V (V6, V8, V12) — two angled banks; short engine, suits many cylinders
Flat / boxer (H4, H6) — horizontally opposed; low centre of gravity (Subaru, Porsche 911)
Rotary, W — rarer designs (Mazda RX-8, VW W12)
vin.info.horsepower:
Peak engine power. 1 hp ≈ 0.746 kW, so 120 hp ≈ 89 kW. US data uses SAE horsepower; European “PS” / “к.с.” (metric hp) is about 1.4% smaller.
Under 100 hp — city cars (Hyundai i10 ≈ 67–87 hp)
100–150 hp — everyday family cars (Kia Ceed 1.6 ≈ 120–130 hp)
150–250 hp — brisk: hot hatches and large SUVs (VW Golf GTI ≈ 245 hp)
250 hp and up — sports cars and big V6/V8 engines (Ford Mustang GT ≈ 450+ hp)
vin.info.kilowatts:
Peak engine power in kilowatts (kW), the SI unit used on European registration papers. 1 kW ≈ 1.34 hp.
50 kW — ≈ 67 hp
75 kW — ≈ 100 hp
100 kW — ≈ 134 hp
150 kW — ≈ 201 hp
vin.info.fuelPrimary: The main fuel: gasoline, diesel, electric, LPG…
vin.info.fuelSecondary: A second fuel the engine can use (e.g. bi-fuel gasoline + LPG).
vin.info.valveTrain:
How the valves that let air in and exhaust out are driven by camshafts.
SOHC (single overhead cam) — one camshaft per bank; simple and compact, common in older and economy engines
DOHC (dual overhead cam) — two camshafts per bank; better airflow and high-rev power, now the norm, usually 4 valves per cylinder
OHV (pushrod) — camshaft in the engine block; compact and torquey, used in many US V8s (Chevrolet small-block)
Variable valve timing (VVT, VTEC, VANOS) is added on top of these to improve efficiency and power.
vin.info.turbo:
A turbocharger uses exhaust gas to force more air into the cylinders, making more power from a smaller engine.
Typical in downsized 1.0–1.5 L petrols (Ford EcoBoost, VW TSI)
Almost every modern diesel is turbocharged
Trade-off: more heat and complexity — wants good oil and a short cool-down after hard driving
vin.info.electrification:
Hybrid or electric system level.
MHEV — mild hybrid: a small 48 V motor assists the engine but cannot drive the car alone (Suzuki Swift Hybrid, many Audi and Mercedes)
HEV — full hybrid: can drive short distances on electricity and charges itself (Toyota Prius, Corolla Hybrid)
PHEV — plug-in hybrid: bigger battery, roughly 40–80 km electric range, charges from the grid (Toyota RAV4 Prime, Volvo T8)
BEV — battery electric: no combustion engine (Tesla Model 3, Nissan Leaf)
FCEV — hydrogen fuel cell (Toyota Mirai)
vin.info.seatBelt: Belt type fitted: manual (you buckle up) or with automatic components.
vin.info.pretensioner: Pyrotechnic device that tightens the belt in the first milliseconds of a crash.
vin.info.tpms: Direct = a pressure sensor inside every wheel. Indirect = estimated from wheel-speed (ABS) data, less precise.
vin.info.airbagFront: Frontal airbags in the steering wheel and dashboard, by seat row.
vin.info.airbagSide: Airbags in the seat or door that protect the torso in a side impact.
vin.info.airbagCurtain: Inflatable curtains along the side windows that protect heads in side impacts and rollovers.
vin.info.airbagKnee: Airbag under the dashboard that protects legs and keeps the occupant in position.
vin.info.abs: Anti-lock braking: stops the wheels locking so you can steer while braking hard.
vin.info.esc: Electronic stability control: brakes individual wheels to stop a skid. Mandatory on new cars in the US and EU.
vin.info.tc: Traction control: limits wheel spin when accelerating on slippery surfaces.
vin.info.fcw: Warns the driver of an imminent frontal collision.
vin.info.dbs: Adds braking force when the driver brakes too lightly to avoid a collision.
vin.info.aeb: Automatic emergency braking that detects pedestrians.
vin.info.acc: Cruise control that keeps a set distance to the vehicle ahead.
vin.info.ldw: Warns when the car drifts out of its lane without signalling.
vin.info.lka: Gently steers the car back into its lane.
vin.info.bsw: Warns of vehicles in the blind spot when changing lanes.
vin.info.rcta: Warns of cross traffic when reversing out of a parking space.
vin.info.keyless: Push-button start with a key fob that stays in your pocket.
vin.info.drl: Lights that switch on automatically in daytime to make the car more visible.

safety.title: Crash safety statistics
safety.unavailable: Safety ratings aren't available right now.
safety.none: No NHTSA rating found — this US-market database rarely covers EU/JDM-spec or Soviet-era vehicles.
safety.coverageNhtsa: Covers vehicles sold new in the US, matched by exact make/model/year. Only reliably covers MY2011 onward (NHTSA's current combined 5-star program) — older model years used different, non-comparable test criteria.
safety.source: Source: NHTSA 5-Star Safety Ratings (USA) — matched by make/model/year, US-spec trims only.
safety.euroncapNone: No Euro NCAP rating found for this make/model.
safety.coverageEuroncap: Covers EU-spec vehicles Euro NCAP actually tested, 2017 onward. A rating expires 6 years after publication (shown as "other tested generations" past that point).
safety.euroncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year — other tested generations are shown below.
safety.euroncapExpired: This rating has expired (Euro NCAP ratings are valid for 6 years from publication).
safety.euroncapSource: Source: Euro NCAP — matched by make/model, EU-spec vehicles.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoStars: 0–5 stars: Euro NCAP's overall safety rating for this tested variant.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoAdultOccupant: Adult Occupant: how well the structure and restraints protect adult occupants in a crash.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoChildOccupant: Child Occupant: protection for children in the car's own child seats, plus how easy it is to fit compatible child seats.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoVulnerableRoad: Vulnerable Road Users: protection for pedestrians and cyclists struck by the car, and how well its systems detect them.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoSafetyAssist: Safety Assist: how much standard-fit tech (autonomous braking, lane assist, speed limiting) helps avoid a crash in the first place.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoSafetyPack: Safety Pack: results for an optional equipment package — the base/Standard trim may score differently.
safety.euroncapRatingsInfoExpiry: Ratings expire after 6 years — Euro NCAP's test protocol gets stricter over time, so an old 5-star rating isn't directly comparable to a new one.
safety.jncapNone: No JNCAP rating found for this make/model — this Japan-domestic database only covers vehicles NASVA actually tested.
safety.coverageJncap: Covers JDM-domestic vehicles NASVA actually tested, 2003 onward (with real gaps: no 2004-2006 or 2008).
safety.jncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year — other tested generations are shown below.
safety.jncapSource: Source: JNCAP (Japan, NASVA) — matched by make/model, JDM-domestic vehicles.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoStars: 0–5 stars: JNCAP's overall safety rating for this tested vehicle.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoPreventive: Preventive safety: how well the car's active-safety tech (autonomous braking, lane assist, headlights) helps avoid a crash — graded A (best) through E.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoCollision: Collision safety: occupant and pedestrian protection in frontal, side, and whiplash tests — graded A (best) through E.
safety.jncapRatingsInfoEmergencyCall: Emergency call system: whether the car automatically alerts emergency services after a serious crash, and how advanced that system is.
safety.cncapNone: No C-NCAP rating found for this make/model — this China-market database only covers vehicles CATARC actually tested.
safety.coverageCncap: Covers China-market vehicles CATARC actually tested, 2006 onward.
safety.cncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year — other tested generations are shown below.
safety.cncapSource: Source: C-NCAP (China, CATARC) — matched by make/model, China-market vehicles.
safety.cncapRatingsInfoUnit: C-NCAP has no star rating — scores before 2018 are raw points with no fixed maximum, and scores from 2018 onward are a clean percentage; the two are never directly comparable.
safety.cncapRatingsInfoOccupant: Occupant protection: how well the structure and restraints protect occupants in a crash.
safety.cncapRatingsInfoVru: Pedestrian/VRU protection: protection for pedestrians and cyclists struck by the car (tested from 2018 onward only).
safety.cncapRatingsInfoActiveSafety: Active safety: how much standard-fit tech helps avoid a crash in the first place (tested from 2018 onward only).
safety.kncapNone: No KNCAP rating found for this make/model — this Korea-market database only covers vehicles KNCAP actually tested.
safety.coverageKncap: Covers Korea-market vehicles KNCAP actually tested, 2021 onward — an older historical corpus exists but isn't in this database yet.
safety.kncapNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year — other tested generations are shown below.
safety.kncapSource: Source: KNCAP (Korea, MOLIT/KoROAD) — matched by make/model, Korea-market vehicles, 2021 onward only.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoClass: Class (1-5): KNCAP's overall safety tier for this tested vehicle — 1 is the best.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoCrash: Crash safety: occupant protection in frontal, side, and pole-impact tests.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoPedestrian: Pedestrian safety: protection for pedestrians struck by the car.
safety.kncapRatingsInfoAccident: Accident-prevention safety: how much standard-fit tech helps avoid a crash in the first place.
safety.iihsNone: No IIHS rating found for this make/model — this US-market database only covers vehicles IIHS actually tested.
safety.coverageIihs: Covers US-market vehicles IIHS actually tested, model year 1994 onward.
safety.iihsNoGenerationMatch: No rating matches this vehicle's model year.
safety.iihsSource: Source: IIHS (US, insurance-industry-funded) — matched by make/model, US-market vehicles, model year 1994 onward only.
safety.iihsRatingsInfoScale: Good/Acceptable/Marginal/Poor: IIHS's crashworthiness scale across small-overlap front, moderate-overlap front, side, and headlight tests.
safety.iihsRatingsInfoFcp: Front crash prevention: Superior/Advanced/Basic on older tests, or Good/Acceptable/Marginal/Poor on newer ones — how well standard-fit tech helps avoid a crash.
safety.iihsRatingsInfoAward: Top Safety Pick / Top Safety Pick+: IIHS's annual award for vehicles meeting its highest combined standards that model year.
safety.coverageInfoIntro: All six sources are supplementary, best-effort matches — none of them guarantees a result for every car, so always check the vehicle's actual specification.
safety.coverageInfoEuroNcapBody: Tests EU-spec cars — the vast majority of Ukraine's registered fleet by brand — but only specific tested trims and generations, not every model or year. A rating only shows up when Euro NCAP actually tested that make/model.
safety.brandsInfoIntro: NHTSA only tests vehicles sold new in the US, matched by exact make/model/year — not every model or year of a covered brand has a rating on file.
safety.brandsInfoDiscontinued: Discontinued in the US (older model years only)
safety.brandsInfoUncovered: Never sold in the US — no rating will ever exist, e.g.
safety.coverageInfoJncapBody: Tests JDM-domestic cars — models never exported to the EU or US, like the Toyota Alphard/Crown/Mark X or Nissan Skyline/Cedric/Elgrand. Only vehicles NASVA actually tested have a rating.
safety.coverageInfoCncapBody: Tests China-market cars — the BYD/Geely/Chery/Zeekr/Haval fleet Ukraine grey-imports in volume — under their China-spec names, translated here from CATARC's own Chinese-language results. Only vehicles CATARC actually tested have a rating.
safety.coverageInfoKncapBody: Tests Korea-domestic cars — Hyundai/Kia/Genesis/KGM EVs and other Korea-only models — under their Korean names, translated here from KNCAP's own results. Only covers 2021 onward, and only vehicles KNCAP actually tested have a rating.
safety.coverageInfoIihsBody: Tests the same US-spec fleet NHTSA does, but on a different methodology (Good/Acceptable/Marginal/Poor across small-overlap, side, and crash-prevention tests, plus Top Safety Pick awards) — a car can rate well on one scale and not the other. Only vehicles IIHS actually tested have a rating.
safety.ratingsInfoStars: 1–5 stars, more stars = safer. "Not Rated" means NHTSA never tested that specific trim.
safety.ratingsInfoOverall: Overall: a combined score across all frontal, side, and rollover tests below.
safety.ratingsInfoFront: Front: driver/passenger protection in a 35 mph frontal crash into a fixed barrier.
safety.ratingsInfoSide: Side: occupant protection in a 38 mph side impact, plus a separate side pole impact test.
safety.ratingsInfoAverage: Average: when a make/model/year has several tested trims (body style, drivetrain), this is the mean across all of them, shown above the individual breakdown.
safety.ratingsInfoRollover: Rollover: risk of a rollover in a single-vehicle loss-of-control event — more stars = lower risk.
safety.ratingsInfoSidePole: Side pole: a separate, more severe side-impact test against a narrow pole (like a tree or post).
safety.ratingsInfoRolloverRisk: Rollover risk %: the actual estimated probability of a rollover, behind the star rating — plus the dynamic test result (e.g. "No Tip") from a real avoidance-maneuver test.
safety.ratingsInfoEquipment: ESC/FCW/LDW: whether stability control, forward-collision warning, and lane-departure warning came standard, optional, or weren't offered on this trim.
safety.ratingsInfoCombinedSideBarrier: Side barrier (combined): an older/secondary side-impact sub-score alongside the main Side and Side pole ratings above.
safety.ratingsInfoComplaints: Complaints/recalls: lifetime counts reported to NHTSA for this vehicle — not part of the crash test itself.
safety.ratingsInfoInvestigations: Investigations: open or closed NHTSA safety investigations into this vehicle.

about.heading: About
about.p1: This app provides vehicle data since January 2013.
about.p2: The information about the vehicles and their owners is taken from the single state open data portal data.gov.ua, managed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine.
about.p3: The single state open data portal was created at the request of the Law of Ukraine “On Access to Public Information” and the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine of October 21, 2015 No. 835 “On Approval of the Regulations on Data Sets to be Disclosed in the Form of Open Data”.
about.p4: The portal is intended to provide access to public information in the form of open data and provides access to information from authorities with the possibility of its subsequent use.
about.p5: Anyone may freely copy, publish, distribute and use public information in the form of open data, including for commercial purposes and in combination with other information or one's own product, provided there is a mandatory link to the source of such information.
about.plateNotice: Since May 2026 (plates are in the database for January 2013 – 29 April 2026), a Ministry of Internal Affairs order (№ 67/ОД) has stopped the portal from publishing plate numbers for new registrations. Where possible, this app reconstructs a vehicle's plate from its own VIN's earlier registration history — such entries are marked as reconstructed.

co2.title: Emissions
co2.infoScore: 0 = clean, 100 = worst. Scored linearly from tailpipe CO₂ (g/km); a pure EV scores 0 because only the tailpipe is counted.
co2.infoCycle: Figures come from the {{cycle}} test cycle; different cycles are not directly comparable (EPA reads lower than WLTP).
co2.infoWltp: WLTP (Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure) is the lab test used for new cars in the EU since 2017–2019. A car is driven on a rolling road through a standard cycle of about 30 minutes — city, suburban, rural and motorway phases up to 131 km/h — which is more realistic than the older NEDC (about 20 minutes, max 120 km/h). EPA is the US procedure; NEDC is the old European one.
co2.infoSources: Data: EEA (European Environment Agency) — official CO₂ monitoring of new cars registered in the EU, from manufacturers' WLTP/NEDC type approvals; EPA (US Environmental Protection Agency) — fuel economy and CO₂ of US-market vehicles, published at fueleconomy.gov.
co2.infoEstimate: An estimate for similar vehicles (same make, model and nearby year) — not a measurement of this exact car. Tap “similar vehicles” to browse them.
co2.noData: No fuel consumption data found for similar vehicles.
fuel.title: Fuel & emissions statistics
fuel.note: Average tailpipe CO₂ (g/km) of similar reference vehicles, weighted by registrations; only cars with a match count. Lower is cleaner. Different test cycles (EPA/NEDC/WLTP) are mixed, so treat it as a rough comparison.
safety.note: Combined crash score (0–100, higher is safer): Euro NCAP, JNCAP, C-NCAP, KNCAP and IIHS results converted to one scale and averaged over the sources that rated a similar car, weighted by registrations. Only cars with a match count. Programmes test differently, so treat it as a rough comparison, not an official rating.

oper.code.13: A typo in the VIN was corrected in the registry card. The car itself did not change.
oper.code.17: First registration of a moped or similar vehicle based on an expert report.
oper.code.18: A departmental record (special signals, dangerous goods, training vehicles) — not a normal owner registration.
oper.code.20: First registration in Ukraine to a private company or organisation.
oper.code.30: First registration in Ukraine to an individual (usually a new car).
oper.code.40: Second-hand car bought from a dealer or trading company and registered anew.
oper.code.48: Used-car registration after a sale contract made at an MIA service centre (after the previous owner deregistered it).
oper.code.49: Used-car registration under a contract made at an MIA service centre.
oper.code.50: Registration of a car under a sale contract; the new owner after the previous one deregistered it.
oper.code.69: Registration by acceptance-transfer deed, typically from a manufacturer/importer to a company.
oper.code.70: Registration of a car imported from abroad, on the customs declaration (ВМД). A "gray import": its first registration in Ukraine, after a previous life abroad. "Б/В" means used.
oper.code.71: Registration of a car imported from abroad, on a customs certificate — also an import via customs.
oper.code.72: Registration of a brand-new car imported from abroad on a customs declaration.
oper.code.80: Registration of a car bought at an auction or commodity exchange.
oper.code.99: First registration of a new, Ukrainian-made car bought from a dealer.
oper.code.100: First registration in Ukraine of a car bought from a trading company and imported ("Б/В" = used) — typical for dealer-imported cars from Europe/US.
oper.code.101: Registration of a car under a lease agreement.
oper.code.105: First registration of a new car bought from a dealer and imported from abroad (e.g. from an official importer).
oper.code.110: Registration of a car received through the social protection office (e.g. for people with disabilities).
oper.code.140: Registration because the car wasn't sold (e.g. it stayed with the dealer).
oper.code.172: First registration of a passenger car imported from abroad.
oper.code.210: A temporary registration slip issued at the owner's request, allowing driving until paperwork is done.
oper.code.212: A temporary slip issued for a re-registration while paperwork is in progress.
oper.code.213: A temporary slip and temporary state registration for the duration of martial law.
oper.code.215: Temporary state registration of a serviceman's car.
oper.code.218: Change of owner via a dealer contract, plus temporary registration for the martial-law period.
oper.code.221: Registration of a car imported under an obligation to re-export it (a temporary import).
oper.code.230: A registration certificate issued for travel abroad. The owner does not change.
oper.code.250: A temporary registration slip issued under a power of attorney — may indicate proxy or temporary use.
oper.code.252: A temporary slip granting the right to drive, issued at the owner's request (usually when someone else drives).
oper.code.254: "Proper user" — a person using the car (e.g. via power of attorney or lease) is recorded; ownership is unchanged.
oper.code.255: A previously issued temporary slip was cancelled.
oper.code.256: A temporary slip was cancelled at the owner's request.
oper.code.270: A temporary slip for mopeds with no registration deadline.
oper.code.284: The "proper user" entry was removed from the registry.
oper.code.307: Change of owner under a sale contract signed in front of a ЦНАП administrator.
oper.code.308: Change of owner under a sale contract with a business (dealer, consignment lot).
oper.code.309: Change of owner by invoice certificate — typically a purchase from a trading company.
oper.code.310: Change of owner under a sale contract notarised by a notary.
oper.code.313: Change of owner via a business contract for a car already registered to that business.
oper.code.314: Change of owner via a sale contract signed online through electronic services (e.g. Diia).
oper.code.315: Change of owner under a contract signed at an MIA service centre — the most common way to buy a used car in Ukraine.
oper.code.317: Change of owner by gift contract signed at an MIA service centre.
oper.code.319: Change of owner by a transfer deed (e.g. between companies).
oper.code.320: Change of owner by a notarised gift contract.
oper.code.321: Change of owner by inheritance — by will or inheritance contract.
oper.code.322: Change of owner by inheritance under law (no will).
oper.code.329: Change of ownership under a financial lease (and buyout of the leased vehicle).
oper.code.330: Change of owner by court decision.
oper.code.331: Change of owner for a car bought at an auction, electronic tender or exchange.
oper.code.340: Re-registration because the owner's details (name, address) changed — same owner, same region.
oper.code.350: Re-registration because the owning company was renamed. Same owner.
oper.code.360: Re-registration with a change of region (the owner moved). Often new plates.
oper.code.363: Re-registration because the car was contributed to a company's charter capital.
oper.code.390: Re-registration because the car's colour was changed (repaint, wrap).
oper.code.400: Re-registration after a modification with no numbered parts changed — most often an LPG/gas installation.
oper.code.402: Re-registration after a modification including an engine swap or type/power change.
oper.code.403: Re-registration after a modification with a new body (chassis) and engine.
oper.code.404: Re-registration after special identification numbers were stamped, or the body number was duplicated.
oper.code.405: Re-registration after special numbers were stamped, or the chassis/frame number was duplicated.
oper.code.408: Re-registration after a modification with no numbered parts changed (e.g. LPG).
oper.code.410: Plate replaced — usually new plates with no change of owner.
oper.code.412: A plate with a chosen digit combination ("vanity plate") was issued.
oper.code.420: Re-registration after a lost plate (a new one was issued).
oper.code.429: Re-registration extending the re-export deadline for a temporarily imported car.
oper.code.430: The registration certificate was replaced. Same owner.
oper.code.434: Owner/address details changed, processed remotely via Diia.
oper.code.440: The registration certificate was lost or a duplicate issued. Same owner.
oper.code.450: The certificate was replaced to correct the car's registry data.
oper.code.520: Deregistered because the car was taken out of Ukraine.
oper.code.530: Deregistered for sale — the owner took the car off the register to sell it, usually right before a change of owner.
oper.code.535: Deregistered under a financial lease contract.
oper.code.536: Deregistered under a contract made at an MIA service centre.
oper.code.537: Deregistered for transfer to a car-trading business.
oper.code.540: Deregistered as scrapped or written off.
oper.code.550: Deregistration of a car imported under a re-export obligation.
oper.code.560: Deregistered on return from a trip abroad (under power of attorney).
oper.code.570: Deregistered because the registering authority changed.
oper.group.reg: A registration event (first, second-hand, or after import). See the operation name for detail.
oper.group.temp: A temporary slip issued or cancelled. Ownership is unchanged.
oper.group.change: Re-registration with no owner change: details, documents, plates or modifications.
oper.group.off: Deregistration — the car is not registered after this (sale, export, scrapping, etc.).
oper.group.other: An administrative registry operation. See the operation name for detail.
oper.catInfo.new: A brand-new car that nobody has used yet: it enters the registry for the first time.
oper.catInfo.import: A used car brought in from abroad: first time in Ukraine, with foreign owners and history outside this registry before that.
oper.catInfo.owner: The owner changed (purchase, inheritance, gift, auction), or the car was first registered to a buyer from a dealer. The key event of the history.
oper.catInfo.modification: The car itself was physically changed: colour, LPG equipment, engine or body. Same owner.
oper.catInfo.deregistered: The car was taken off the register: sold (deregistered for sale), exported or scrapped. It stays unregistered until a new registration appears.
oper.catInfo.noise: Administrative operation: same owner and same car (slips, documents, plates, owner details). Not important for the car’s history.
